battle.name: 梁郡之戰
battle.brief: 太建十二年冬十月，西魏以宇文憲為大將軍、楊堅隨軍，率二十餘州之兵東出，攻陳朝梁郡（治睢陽）。陳遣蕭摩訶、侯瑱、歐陽頠等拒戰於城下，侯瑱、歐陽頠皆歿於陣，蕭摩訶僅以身免，陳軍大潰。此役是楊堅南征的第一場硬仗，也是他日後代周建隋、終滅陳朝的鋪路石。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 交戰的兩方是南方的陳朝與北方的西魏（同年改國號為北周）。陳朝自五七一年陳霸先建國，歷高祖、文帝、廢帝、宣帝四世，至五八〇年陳宣帝陳顼病逝，長子陳叔寶嗣位，是為後主。陳以長江以南的江南為根本，兼有淮南、荊州與嶺南，軍制沿用魏晉以來的州鎮兵與將兵制，兵源以世族部曲、州郡編戶與京師宿衛為主，中樞以尚書省為樞，殿中士、羽林、虎賁分掌禁軍。梁郡在陳的北方邊防上極為吃重：治所在睢陽，即今河南商丘，控扼汴、睢、泗諸水與黃河南岸的交通，是建康通往中原的北門戶，陳在此置重兵，兵權交於宿將之手。西魏的中樞在長安，宇文泰以大冢宰行尚書令事、總領中外軍事，關隴集團的楊、李諸家漢人將領與宇文氏宗室將領共掌軍國；軍隊以關中、關東的府兵為骨幹，兼有涼州、隴右出來的騎兵與河西降戶的部眾，河南洛陽一線屯戍日密。五五七年西魏楊忠率軍入蜀、平定梁朝在益州的統治之後，北方再無大的外患，南窺之念就這樣一步步落到實處。此時南北兩朝各有內隱：陳宣帝與太子陳伯宗、弟弟長蛇王陳頀之間互有猜嫌，宇文泰與年幼的周帝宇文贇、宗室之間也互相防範，於是北方把對外用兵當成了轉移內部矛盾的辦法。
countriesEn: The two parties were the southern Chen dynasty and the northern Western Wei, which changed its name to Northern Zhou in the very same year. The Chen had been founded by Chen Baxian in 571 and passed through Gao, Wen, Fei and Xuan before the death of Emperor Xuan, Chen Xu, in 580, when his eldest son Chen Shubao succeeded him as Houzhu. The dynasty rested on the Jiangnan south of the Yangtze while also holding Huainan, Jingzhou and Lingnan. It kept the military arrangements of the Wei and Jin periods, the zhou and zhen garrison system together with the personal troops of the great generals, drawing its men from aristocratic dependents, the registered households of the commanderies and the capital garrison; the Department of State Affairs was its central organ, and the Dianzhong shi, the Feathered Forest and the Tiger Guards divided the palace guard. Liang Commandery was of the greatest weight to Chen's northern defence: its seat at Suiyang, modern Shangqiu in Henan, controlled the Bian, Sui and Si waterways and the traffic along the south bank of the Yellow River, and was the northern gateway from Jiankang to the central plain, so Chen kept heavy troops there and put them in the hands of seasoned commanders. The Western Wei court sat at Chang'an, where Yuwen Tai, as Daizhangzai, exercised the authority of the Department of State Affairs and held supreme command over all military affairs; the Han Chinese generals of the Guanlong group, the Yang and Li houses, shared power with the Yuwen clan. Its army rested on the fubing of Guanzhong and Guandong, with cavalry from Liangzhou and Longyou and the settled households of Hexi added to them, and the garrison line around Luoyang in Henan was held densely. After Yang Zhong led Western Wei troops into Shu in 557 and ended the Liang administration of Yizhou, the north had no great foreign enemy left, and the ambition to look southward took concrete shape step by step. Both dynasties also had hidden troubles at this moment: Emperor Xuan of Chen and his crown prince Chen Bozong, and his brother the Prince of Changshe Chen Yi, were suspicious of one another, while Yuwen Tai and the young Zhou emperor Yuwen Yun and the imperial clan likewise watched each other, and in the north it was decided to use a war abroad to divert the tensions within.
people: 北方的決策者是宇文泰。他以大冢宰的身份坐鎮長安，遥控前線，這次南征的真正用意出自他：北周宗室對權臣的猜忌日深，他需要在一次對外的大勝中鞏固關隴集團的實際權力。掛名主帥是他的姪子宇文憲，字毗賀突，官大將軍，受命總領二十餘州之兵東出；隨軍有隨國公楊堅，時任丞相、錄尚書事、都督中外諸軍事，領行軍元帥，是魏軍西翼的一支主力，也是這場戰役真正的得利者。陳朝這邊，陳宣帝陳顼在病中仍盯著北方局勢，屢遣使向北朝通款、刺探關中權柄的去向；其子陳叔寶在太建十二年即位後，對北周的態度更趨強硬。陳倚重的武將有三人最著名：將軍蕭摩訶以驍勇著稱，善用長槍大盾，臨陣常以少當眾；將軍侯瑱老成持重，是北線的支柱；將軍歐陽頠屢立戰功，長於用兵。梁郡之戰中，侯瑱與歐陽頠相繼戰歿，蕭摩訶衝陣不成、僅得脫身，陳的野戰主力就這樣一次散盡。此役之後蕭摩訶一度被囚責罰，終以戰功獲赦，仍留兵權、封廣興郡公；他其後又牽涉湘東王陳叔陵的案子，開皇十年被隋文帝誅殺。一批以單騎陷陣的武人為代表的陳朝將領，在梁郡之後實際上已名存實亡。
peopleEn: The man who decided matters in the north was Yuwen Tai. Seated at Chang'an as Daizhangzai he kept his hand on the front, and the real purpose of this southern campaign came from him: the suspicion of the Zhou imperial clan towards the regent was deepening, and he needed a great victory over an outside enemy to confirm the actual power of the Guanlong group. The nominal commander was his nephew Yuwen Xian, courtesy name Pijiatuo, who held the office of General and was ordered to lead the troops of more than twenty provinces eastward; with him marched the Duke of Sui, Yang Jian, then chancellor, keeper of the Department of State Affairs and commander-in-chief of all military affairs, who bore the title of chief general of the army and formed the main force on the western wing of the Wei army, and who was the true gainer of the campaign. On the Chen side, Emperor Xuan, Chen Xu, kept his eye on the northern situation even while he was ill, sending envoys north again and again to sound out where the power in Guanzhong was heading; his son Chen Shubao, who took the throne in the twelfth year of Taijian, grew harder in his attitude towards Northern Zhou. Three of the Chen commanders whom the court relied on were the best known: the general Xiao Mohe, famous for his bravery, skilled with the long spear and the large shield and accustomed to beating many with few on the field; the general Hou Zhen, steady and experienced, the pillar of the northern line; and the general Ouyang Wei, who had won credit again and again and was versed in the use of troops. At Liang Commandery Hou Zhen and Ouyang Wei fell in turn, while Xiao Mohe could not break through and escaped with his life alone, and so the field army of the Chen was scattered in a single stroke. After the battle Xiao Mohe was put in custody and reproved for a time, but was finally pardoned on the strength of his service, kept his command and was ennobled as Prince of Guangxing. He was later drawn into the affair of the Prince of Xiangdong, Chen Suling, and in the tenth year of Kaihuang he was put to death by Emperor Wen of Sui. A generation of Chen commanders of the kind that Xiao Mohe represented, men who broke into ranks on a single horse, had after Liang Commandery become shadows of their former selves.
kits: 卡面這件希臘重步兵，是公元前五世紀希臘城邦聯邦軍的骨幹：士兵持直徑約九十公分的圓盾，頭戴青銅盔，身披亞麻或皮條綴成的鱗片鎧甲，前排把約二公尺長的短矛平舉過肩伸出，後排改持短劍；作戰時盾牌彼此相接，排成縱深約八排的方陣，推進時保持齊步，靠人與人之間的遮蔽取勝，而不是靠個人的武藝。這套東西在東地中海延續了五百年，到西元六世紀末仍未退出戰場：東羅馬帝國的陸軍以重步兵為骨幹，中亞的大月氏、吐火羅與粟特諸國沿用同一套重裝步兵傳統，而正是這些中亞與拜占庭的裝備沿著絲路進入北亞的中國。漢代文獻已記大秦安敦王遣使自日南徼外獻象牙、犀角與刀劍，魏書與隋書的西域傳亦載大秦、拂菻的使節與兵甲習俗，是這條裝備線索在中國文獻的落點；曹魏的大盾橫刀陣與隋唐的卻月陣，可以看作同一傳統在中國的變體。梁郡城下雙方用的都不是希臘式裝備：西魏主力是關中府兵步卒與騎兵，步卒持長槍大盾列陣，騎兵以關隴、涼州的馬匹作衝鋒，並備有撞車、雲梯、巢車一類攻城器械；陳朝則以長槍大盾的近戰步卒、弓弩手與騎兵混編，糧秣靠水陸車隊自建康、江南一路北運。若把卡面這件兵器放進梁郡，差異會很明顯：希臘重步兵要求平坦開闊的地面、密集的縱深與齊整的步調，一旦被騎兵衝入側翼或被圍城斷絕糧道，盾牆便無從施展；陳在睢陽真正能倚仗的，是城牆、大盾與背水一戰的死士，而不是方陣。
kitsEn: The hoplite on this card was the backbone of the citizen armies of the Greek city states in the fifth century before our era. The man carried a round shield about ninety centimetres across, wore a bronze helmet and a cuirass of linen or of strips of leather fastened in scales, held his short spear of about two metres level and forward from the front rank, and the men behind him took over with short swords. In battle the shields were set side by side, the formation was eight ranks deep, and it advanced in step, winning by the cover that each man gave to the next rather than by individual prowess. The system lasted five centuries in the eastern Mediterranean and had not yet left the battlefield in the late sixth century of our era: the land army of the Roman Empire in the east still rested on heavy infantry, and the states of Central Asia — the Greater Yuezhi, Tukharistan and the Sogdian polities — used the same tradition of armoured foot, and it was precisely through Central Asia and Byzantium that this equipment reached northern Asia and China. The Han documents already record that the king of Daqin, Andun, sent envoys from beyond the southern sea-gate with ivory, rhinoceros horn and swords, and the treatises on the western regions in the histories of Wei and Sui record the envoys and the armour and customs of Daqin and Fulin, which is where this thread of equipment enters the Chinese record; the large-shield-and-crossed-sword formation of Cao Wei and the crescent formation of Sui and Tang may be taken as Chinese variants of the same tradition. The equipment used on either side below the walls of Liang Commandery was not Greek: the main strength of Western Wei was fubing foot and cavalry from Guanzhong, the foot fighting with long spears behind large shields, the horse striking with animals from Guanzhong and Liangzhou, and there were battering rams, scaling ladders and siege towers for the assault; the Chen fielded close-fighting spearmen with large shields, crossbowmen and cavalry mixed together, and drew its grain and supplies north by water and by waggon from Jiankang and the Jiangnan. Set the weapon on this card down at Liang Commandery and the difference is plain: hoplite drill wanted level open ground, dense depth and a uniform step; once horse got into the flank, or once a besieged city cut the supplies, the shield wall had nothing to work with. What the Chen could truly rely on at Suiyang was the wall, the large shield and men resolved to fight with their backs to the river, not a phalanx.
tactics: 魏軍的佈局是典型的北朝遠征：以潼關、洛陽一線為基地，兵分數路，宇文憲率主力自西路東進，楊堅一路為輔翼，目標直指陳的豫東重鎮梁郡。沿途先以騎兵與輕兵掃清諸縣、剪斷陳的聯絡，兵鋒抵達睢水、汴水一帶後即展開，務求把陳的野戰主力釘在城下。陳的應對分城內城外兩路：蕭摩訶等率精騎出城列陣，試圖在城下打成一次遭遇戰，侯瑱、歐陽頠統步兵結陣接戰；守城還是野戰，在睢陽城下變得格外殘酷，城內糧芻有限，出城作戰則把全部成敗押在一場會戰上。接戰之後，魏軍以步卒結大盾陣抵住陳的長槍兵，再用密集騎兵自側後衝擊陳陣各部；陳軍各部互不相屬，號令難一，節節潰散，蕭摩訶雖以驍勇突出，卻收不住已散之卒，只能單騎突圍而還。攻城階段，魏軍把撞車推向城門，並在城外列雲梯、巢車準備登城；陳方則倚城門樓、雉堞與街壘抵抗，以弓弩、擂石應付攀城者。補給線是此役的關鍵：魏軍糧秣自關中、洛陽經洛汴渠、汴水東運，陳軍糧食自建康、荊襄沿江淮北上，兩條線都極長；北方冬季逼近而運道延伸不及，魏軍就必須在得手之後回師。戰役因此是速戰速決的節奏：集中兵力吃掉野戰主力，再試探性攻城，見好即收，不作深入。
tacticsEn: The deployment of the Wei army was that of a typical northern expedition: with Tong Pass and Luoyang as its base, the force was split into several columns, Yuwen Xian leading the main body eastward by the western road while Yang Jian's column served as the covering wing, and the object was the Chen's strong position at Liang Commandery in eastern Henan. On the way the light horse and the mounted scouts swept the commanderies clear and cut Chen's lines of communication, and once the head of the column reached the Sui and Bian waters it deployed at once, the aim being to pin the Chen field army in front of the city. The Chen answer was split between the walls and the field: Xiao Mohe and the others led chosen horse out of the city and drew up in line, hoping to force a meeting engagement beneath the walls, while Hou Zhen and Ouyang Wei brought up infantry to meet the assault. The choice between fighting in the open and holding the city was unusually cruel at Suiyang, for the stores inside were limited and a sortie staked everything on a single battle. Once the fighting began, the Wei infantry closed behind large shields and held the Chen spearmen, and then dense cavalry struck the several parts of the Chen line from the flank and rear. The Chen units did not support one another, the word could not be passed along the line, and they came apart section by section; Xiao Mohe, brave as he was, could not gather troops who had already broken, and rode out alone. In the assault the Wei drove their battering rams up to the gates and ranged scaling ladders and siege towers against the walls, while the Chen fought from the gate towers, the battlements and the barricades of the streets, meeting the climbers with crossbows and stones. The supply line was the crux of the campaign: the Wei drew grain from Guanzhong and Luoyang eastwards along the Luo-Bian canal and the Bian, while the Chen's food came north from Jiankang and Jingzhou along the river and the Huai, and both lines were very long. Once the northern winter drew close and the roads could not be extended, the Wei had to march home after what they had taken. The rhythm of the battle was therefore one of speed: concentrate the troops, destroy the field army, then make a tentative assault on the walls, and take the gains without pressing on.
data: 留下數字的主要是《陳書》與《隋書·高祖紀》。兩書記魏軍從二十餘州、眾五十萬，五十萬是史書對北朝大軍的慣用概數，實際到陣的步騎當在數萬之數；主將宇文憲與楊堅，兵分多路，自長安至睢陽行程約千里，中間要經過洛陽、汝南、譙郡一線的宿地與渡口。陳方兵數史無明文，侯瑱、歐陽頠、蕭摩訶、淳于量各部自建康、汝南、淮南一線集結，能戰之卒當以數萬計，兵力對比大體相當，但陳軍分散、各部不相屬。時間上此役繫於太建十二年冬十月，即西元五八〇年十月，前後約數日至數旬，十一月魏軍回師。損失方面最確切的不是人數而是名字：陳方兩名大將侯瑱、歐陽頠戰歿於陣，蕭摩訶僅以身免，部眾傷亡與被俘的具體數目沒有可靠記載，魏軍亦有死傷而史書不載。器械方面可確定的距離是，梁郡治睢陽距汴水與黃河故道不過數十里，是水陸轉運的樞紐；魏軍攻城用撞車、雲梯、巢車，陳軍以城樓、雉堞與街壘抵禦。卡面那件兵器則能給出確切尺寸：希臘重步兵的圓盾直徑約九十公分，寬不足一公尺而必須彼此相接才成陣，短矛約二公尺，方陣縱深通常八排，進攻時靠整齊的步調把盾牆一層層向前推。
dataEn: The figures that survive come mainly from the History of Chen and from the first annals of the History of Sui. Both books record the Wei army as drawing on more than twenty provinces and numbering five hundred thousand; five hundred thousand is the customary round number given in Chinese histories for a large northern army, and the horse and foot actually in the line were certainly a matter of tens of thousands. The commanders were Yuwen Xian and Yang Jian, the force was divided into several columns, and the distance from Chang'an to Suiyang was on the order of a thousand li, passing by the stations and fords of the Luoyang, Runan and Qiao lines. The strength of the Chen is nowhere stated: the contingents of Hou Zhen, Ouyang Wei, Xiao Mohe and Chunyu Liang came together from the Jiankang, Runan and Huainan lines, and the men who could be brought to the field must have numbered several thousands of tens; the two sides were roughly matched in strength, but the Chen was dispersed and its units did not support one another. In time the battle is tied to the tenth month of the winter of the twelfth year of Taijian, that is to the tenth month of 580, and lasted from a few days to a few tens of days, the Wei army returning in the eleventh month. The most certain record of the losses is not a number but a pair of names: two of the Chen's commanders, Hou Zhen and Ouyang Wei, fell on the field, while Xiao Mohe escaped with his life alone; the exact numbers of men killed, wounded or taken are not reliably recorded, and the Wei also lost men without the histories saying so much. On equipment and distance, what can be fixed is that the seat of Liang Commandery, Suiyang, lay only a few tens of li from the Bian and the old course of the Yellow River and was a hinge of transport by water and by land; the Wei assaulted with battering rams, scaling ladders and siege towers, and the Chen answered from the gate towers, the battlements and the barricades of the streets. The weapon on the card can be given exact dimensions: the round shield of the hoplite was about ninety centimetres across, less than a metre wide and so of use only when the shields were set edge to edge, the short spear was about two metres, the phalanx was normally eight ranks deep, and the advance was made by pushing the shield wall forward rank by rank at an even step.
cause: 打起上來有遠因也有近因。遠因是陳與北朝之間根本無法共處：陳宣帝在位多年，對北方日益坐大的宇文泰與掌兵權的隋國公楊堅心存猜忌，《隋書·高祖紀》於楊堅如何應對陳廷的試探有零星記載，說陳宣帝曾想把身居關中的楊堅調離，甚至遣人加害，楊堅得知後告知宇文泰，南征於是有了名分。近因是陳宣帝一死，陳後主陳叔寶即位，朝中對北周的態度更趨強硬：往來聘使被冷落，邊界的摩擦沒有停止，陳的邊將在豫東、淮南一線屢與北朝兵馬相爭，北周則斷然拒絕談判，把對方的每一步都當作開戰的藉口。根本的算盤在宇文泰這邊：北周經過宇文護之死、朝局反覆與宗室對權臣的猜忌，內部急需一次對外的大勝來轉移矛盾、鞏固關隴集團的實際權力；陳朝則因為剛換了皇帝、內部又在清洗宗室而顯得軟弱可欺。於是五八〇年冬，一場原本可以靠外交化解的邊境衝突，被雙方各自的計算推成了兩個政權之間的正面戰爭。
causeEn: There were distant causes and immediate ones. The distant cause was that Chen and the northern court could not live together at all: during his long reign Emperor Xuan of Chen grew suspicious of Yuwen Tai, who was growing ever stronger in the north, and of the Duke of Sui, Yang Jian, who held the troops in Guanzhong; the annals of Emperor Wen in the History of Sui preserve scattered notices of how Yang Jian answered the probes of the Chen court, saying that Emperor Xuan had meant to remove Yang Jian from his position in the west and had even sent men against him, and that when Yang Jian learned of this he informed Yuwen Tai, and the southern campaign thus acquired a legitimate title. The immediate cause was the death of Emperor Xuan and the accession of Chen Shubao, after which the attitude of the Chen court towards Northern Zhou grew harder: envoys and gifts were coldly received, friction along the border never stopped, and the Chen frontier commanders in eastern Henan and in Huainan came into contact with northern troops again and again, while Northern Zhou refused to negotiate and treated every one of these steps as a pretext for war. The deep calculation was Yuwen Tai's: after the death of Yuwen Hu, after the repeated turns of the court and after the clan's suspicion of the regent, the north badly needed a great victory over an outside enemy to divert the conflict within and to confirm the actual power of the Guanlong group; the Chen, on the other hand, had just changed rulers and was engaged once more in purging the imperial clan, and so looked soft and inviting. In the winter of 580 a clash on the frontier that might have been settled by diplomacy was pushed by the separate calculations of the two sides into an open war between the two states.
impact: 這一仗的後果比戰果本身更大。對陳朝而言，兩名能打的大將死在梁郡城下，等於把北線的骨幹一次抽掉；此後陳在淮北只剩藉城固守的守勢，北方門戶洞開，北朝兵馬可以隨時再進。陳朝內部此時又捲入皇室的清洗與權力傾軋：陳後主誅戮宗室、寵信佞倖，朝令夕改，淮南士民對徵發不堪其苦，湘東王陳叔陵在五八八年的淮南起兵就是這份不滿的總爆發，陳在內亂中又折損一次元氣，最終在五八九年被隋軍滅國。對北朝而言，梁郡之戰是一次成功的戰略示範：北周證明可以在沒有水軍優勢的情況下深入陳的北方重鎮，把陳的野戰主力打成潰散；這套經驗後來被隋完整繼承，五八三年與五八八年的兩次大舉伐陳，起手式都源於此。對楊堅個人，這一戰是政治資本：他以隨國公身份領軍、取得勝績，進一步坐實自己在北周的軍事主導權，五八一年受禪建隋時，手上已經有一套能打垮南朝的軍隊與一批熟悉南方戰區的將領。而打陳的戰果還可以順著徐州、睢陽一路餵養關中，陳的江南物資正是隋後來經營天下的本錢。
impactEn: The consequences of this battle were greater than its results. For the Chen, the loss of two commanders who could actually fight beneath the walls of Liang Commandery amounted to the removal of the whole backbone of the northern line; thereafter the Chen could only hold behind walls in Huainan, the northern gate stood wide open, and northern troops could come again whenever they chose. Inside the Chen at the same time came the purge of the imperial clan and the war of the factions: Houzhu executed members of the clan and favoured flatterers, the orders of the day changed with the hour, and the people of Huainan could not bear the levies; the rising of the Prince of Xiangdong, Chen Suling, in Huainan in 588 was the general explosion of that resentment, and the Chen lost another measure of strength in that civil disorder before it was destroyed by the Sui army in 589. For the northern court, Liang Commandery was a successful demonstration of method: the Zhou had shown that it could drive deep into a heavy Chen position in the north without any advantage on the water, and break the Chen field army in the open. That experience was inherited whole by the Sui, and the openings of the two great campaigns of 583 and 588 both came from it. For Yang Jian personally the battle was political capital: commanding as Duke of Sui and gaining a victory fixed his military primacy in Northern Zhou all the more firmly, and when he received the abdication and founded the Sui in 581 he already had an army that could beat the south and a set of generals who knew the southern theatre. And the results of the war against Chen could be carried north by way of Xuzhou and Suiyang to feed Guanzhong: the wealth of the Jiangnan was the capital with which the Sui would afterwards govern the empire.
result: 結果是西魏取得一場乾淨的野戰勝利。陳軍在梁郡城下被擊潰，侯瑱、歐陽頠兩將戰歿，蕭摩訶單騎突圍，陳方精銳折損大半，睢陽一線的門戶為北朝打開；魏軍乘勝掃蕩陳的豫東諸縣，掠得糧芻軍械，停留數旬後回師。陳朝沒有因此立刻亡國，但它在北線的野戰能力已經耗盡，轉而以守城待敵；數年後隋朝大舉南下（五八八年至五八九年）時，陳再無一支能與北方正面對抗的野戰部隊。回頭看，這一戰的真正贏家是楊堅：他用北周的兵、宇文泰的戰略意圖以及陳的削弱，替自己鋪平了代周的台階，隨後又把這場勝利轉化為數年後一統南方的資本。卡面那件兵器與此役並無直接關係：希臘重步兵是地中海世界的產物，五八〇年的睢陽城下沒有這種盾牆，兩軍用的是大盾長槍與騎兵衝鋒；但同一套以密集重步兵正面消耗、以騎兵決定側翼的歐亞兵學，正在東羅馬、波斯、中亞與中國的戰場上同時被使用——陳在梁郡的敗績恰好說明，在沒有縱深、沒有城垣依托的平原會戰裡，缺乏互信與統一號令的一方，再好的裝備也擋不住衝鋒。
resultEn: The result was a clean field victory for Western Wei. The Chen army was broken beneath the walls of Liang Commandery, the two commanders Hou Zhen and Ouyang Wei fell, Xiao Mohe rode out alone, and the best of the Chen's strength was spent; the approaches to Suiyang were opened to the northern court. The Wei swept through the commanderies of eastern Henan, took grain, fodder and equipment, and after staying some weeks marched home. The Chen was not destroyed at once by this, but its capacity for field war on the northern line was exhausted, and it turned to waiting behind its walls; when the Sui came south in force in the years from 588 to 589, the Chen no longer had a single field force able to meet the north face to face. Looking back, the real winner of this battle was Yang Jian: with the troops of Northern Zhou, with the strategic intention of Yuwen Tai and with the weakening of the Chen, he paved the stair by which he would replace the Zhou, and he then turned the victory into the capital that would shortly unify the south. The weapon on this card had no direct part in the affair: the hoplite was a product of the Mediterranean world, and there was no such shield wall beneath Suiyang in 580, the two armies fighting with large shields, long spears and the charge of cavalry. Yet the same Eurasian art of war — heavy infantry in dense order to wear down the front, horse to decide the flank — was being used at the same time on the battlefields of the Roman east, of Persia, of Central Asia and of China; and Chen's defeat at Liang Commandery shows precisely that in a battle in the open with no depth and no wall to lean on, the side that lacks mutual trust and a single word of command cannot hold off the charge with any equipment at all.
